s: Which one of the following National Parks has a climate that varies from tropical subtropical, temperate and arctic?
x: It is located between the Dapha bum range of the Mishmi Hills and the Patkai range. It is crossed by the Noa Dihing River (a tributary of the Brahmaputra River) that originates at Chaukan Pass. It is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot. It encompasses a wide variety of vegetation, including evergreen, moist deciduous, subtropical, temperate, and alpine forests, owing to its diverse altitudes and climatic zones. It is the only park in the World to have all four feline big cat species: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard, and Clouded Leopard. It is famous for the critically endangered Namdapha flying squirrel, which is endemic to the park. • Major Fauna: Asian wild dog (dhole), Malayan sun bear, Indian wolf, Asiatic black bear, red panda, red fox, Asian golden cat, Indian elephant, wild boar, musk deer, hog deer, sambar, gaur, takin, bharal (blue sheep). • Primates: Stump-tailed macaque, slow loris, Western Hoolock gibbon (the only 'ape' species found in India), capped langur, Assamese macaque and rhesus macaque.

s: Which one of the following protected areas is well known for the conservation of a sub-species of the Indian swamp deer (Barasingha) that thrives well on hard ground and is exclusively graminivorous?
x: Hard ground swamp deer (Barasingha or Rucervus duvaucelii, IUCN: VU) is the state animal of Madhya Pradesh. It has seen a revival in the Kanha National Park and Tiger Reserve (KNPTR) after near-extinction. Successful breeding programs and conservation efforts helped in the species' recovery at KNPTR. Swamp deer are extinct in Pakistan and Bangladesh, now found only in southwestern Nepal and central/northeastern India. There are three subspecies of swamp deer in the Indian Subcontinent:  Western swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii) found in Nepal.  Southern swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii branderi) found in central and north India.  Eastern swamp deer (Rucervus duvaucelii ranjitsinhi) found in Kaziranga and Dudhwa National Parks.

s: Kanha National park is famous for
x: The Kanha National Park in Madhya Pradesh came into being in 1955 and forms the core of the Kanha Tiger Reserve, created in 1973-74 under Project Tiger. The Park's landmark achievement is the preservation of the rare hardground Swamp Deer (Barasingha), saving it from near extinction. Stringent conservation programs for the overall protection of the Park's fauna and flora, makes Kanha one of the most well maintained National Parks in Asia.

s: Dhoopgarh Peak is situated in which of the following National Parks?

s: Kanha National Park belongs to which one among the following biogeographical areas in the world?

s: Two important rivers - one with its source in Jharkhand (and known by a different name in Odisha), and another, with its source in Odishamerge at a place only a short distance from the coast of Bay of Bengal before flowing into the sea. This is an important site of wildlife and biodiversity and a protected area. Which one of the following could be this?
x: South Koel River rises in the Chota Nagpur Plateau of Jharkhand and flows southeastward before joining the Sankh River near Rourkela in Odisha, forming the Brahmani River. The Baitarani River originates in the Keonjhar district of Odisha and flows eastward across the state. Before draining into the Bay of Bengal, the Brahmani and Baitarani rivers converge in the coastal plains of Odisha, creating an extensive estuarine delta system. This deltaic region encompasses the Bhitarkanika National Park.

s: Which of the following National Parks is unique in being a swamp with floating vegetation that supports a rich biodiversity?
x: Keibul Lamjao National Park is the only floating park in the world. It is an integral part of Loktak Lake (a Ramsar site). The National Park is characterised by floating decomposed plant materials locally called phumdis. It was declared a National Park to preserve the natural refuge of brow-antlered deer (also called sangai, dancing deer & Manipur's Eld's deer; EN). Vegetation: semi-evergreen forests, aquatic, and wetland. Major Fauna: brow-antlered deer, hog deer, large Indian civet, Asian golden cat.

s: Which of the following National Parks is unique in being swamp with floating vegetation that supports a rich biodiversity?
x: The Keibul Lamjao National Park is situated in Bishnupur district of Manipur. This national park is characterized by many floating decomposed plant materials locally called phumdis.

s: Keibul Lamjao National Park is located in which lake?

s: UNESCO has approved the inclusion of ‘Himalayan National Park’ in the World’s heritage sites in June 2014. It is situated in :
x: One of the national parks of India, ‘Great Himalayan National Park’ is located in the Kullu region of Himachal Pradesh. In 2014, the ‘Great Himalayan National Park Conservation Area’ has been included in the World Heritage Site (Natural Category) and ‘Rani-Ki-Vav’- Patan, Gujarat has been included in the world heritage of cultural category. In the year 2016, the archaeological sites of Nalanda Mahavihara (Nalanda University), Chandigarh’s historic capital complex (Complex Du Capitole) and Sikkim’s Kanchenjunga National Park were also included in this list. In 2023, two more sites- Karnataka's Hoysala temples (42nd site) & West Bengal's Shantiniketan (41st site) have been added to World Heritage sites, by UNESCO. It is worth mentioning that Moidams - the Mound- Burial system of the Ahom Dynasty was added in the list in 2024. In the year 2025 Maratha Military Landscapes (44th site) has been added to World Heritage sites by UNESCO. At present there are of 44 World Heritage sites in India (36 Cultural Categories, 7 Natural categories and 1 Mixed category).

s: Great Himalayan National Park, which has been accorded the UNESCO World Heritage Site status, is located in:

s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Nokrek Biosphere Reserve Garo Hills
2. Loktak Lake Barail Range
3. Namdapha National Park Dafla Hills
Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
x: Pair 1 is correct: Nokrek Biosphere Reserve is located in northeast India, on the Tura Range, which forms part of the Meghalaya Plateau (average altitude: 600 metres). The entire area is mountainous, and Nokrek is the highest peak of the Garo hills, rising up 1,412 metres. Vegetation: Evergreen, semi-evergreen & deciduous. Pair 2 is incorrect: Loktak Lake is a freshwater lake in Manipur. It is the largest freshwater lake in the northeastern region. Keibul Lamjao, the only floating national park in the world, floats over it. Thick, floating mats of weeds covered with soil (phumids) are a characteristic feature. It is not located in the Barail Range. The Barail Range is the highest hill range in Assam and serves as the watershed separating the Brahmaputra and Barak river systems. Pair 3 is incorrect: It is located in Arunachal Pradesh between the Dapha Bum range of the Mishmi Hills and the Patkai range. It is crossed by the Noa Dihing River (a tributary of the Brahmaputra River) that originates at Chaukan Pass. It is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot. It is the only park in the World to have the four Feline species of big cat, namely: Tiger, Leopard, Snow Leopard and Clouded Leopard. It is famous for the critically endangered Namdapha flying squirrel, which is endemic to the park. Vegetation: Evergreen to temperate broadleaf forest. • Daphla (or Dafla) Hills is a tract of hilly country on the border of western Arunachal and Assam.

Which of the above pairs is/are correctly matched?
x: Nokrek National Park is located 2 km from Tura Peak in West Garo Hills district of Meghalaya. UNESCO added this park to its list of Biosphere Reserves in May, 2009. Loktak Lake is the largest freshwater lake of India. It is located in Manipur and is famous for the phumdis floating over it. Namdapha National Park is the largest protected area in the Eastern Himalaya biodiversity hotspot and is located in Arunachal Pradesh.
